name: AcSysCmdAction
description: Used with the SysCmd method to specify an action to take.

constants.name: acSysCmdInitMeter
constants.description: Initializes the progress meter. You must specify the argument1 and argument2 arguments when you use this action.

constants.name: acSysCmdUpdateMeter
constants.description: Updates the progress meter with the specified value. You must specify the text argument when you use this action.

constants.name: acSysCmdRemoveMeter
constants.description: Removes the progress meter.

constants.name: acSysCmdSetStatus
constants.description: Sets the status bar text to the text argument.

constants.name: acSysCmdClearStatus
constants.description: Provides information on the state of a database object.

constants.name: acSysCmdRuntime
constants.description: Returns True (1) if a run-time version of Microsoft Access is running.

constants.name: acSysCmdAccessVer
constants.description: Returns the version number of Microsoft Access.

constants.name: acSysCmdIniFile
constants.description: Returns the name of the .ini file associated with Microsoft Access.

constants.name: acSysCmdAccessDir
constants.description: Returns the name of the directory where Msaccess.exe is located.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetObjectState
constants.description: Returns the state of the specified database object. You must specify argument1 and argument2 when you use this action value.

constants.name: acSysCmdClearHelpTopic
constants.description: Resets default help topic.

constants.name: acSysCmdProfile
constants.description: Returns the \/profile setting specified by the user when starting Microsoft Access from the command line.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetWorkgroupFile
constants.description: Returns the path to the workgroup file (System.mdw).

constants.name: acSysCmdCompile
constants.description: Compiles the Visual Basic code modules in the current database. Equivalent to the Debug > Compile menu command.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetMsoBuildNumber
constants.description: Returns the build number of the shared MSO component as a Long. This is the same value returned by Application.Build, and it may differ from the Access application build. Use acSysCmdGetBuildNumber (725) in new code to get the Access build number.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetFullVersion
constants.description: Returns a display string containing version, build, channel, and bitness (for example, "Microsoft Access (Version 2601) Build 16.0.19628.20000 Current Channel 64-bit"). Version 2604 and later.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetVersion
constants.description: Returns the short YYMM marketing version (for example, "2601"). Version 2604 and later.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetFullBuildNumber
constants.description: Returns the full four-part build string (for example, "16.0.19916.30000"). Version 2604 and later.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetChannelName
constants.description: Returns the update channel name (for example, "Current Channel", "Monthly Enterprise Channel", or "LTSC 2024"). Version 2604 and later.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetBitness
constants.description: Returns "32-bit" or "64-bit" as a string matching the bitness of the running binary. Version 2604 and later.

constants.name: acSysCmdGetBuildNumber
constants.description: Returns the major build number (for example, 19916) as a Long. Version 2604 and later.
